name: VBG Group AB
reason: Truck/trailer couplings and bus climate systems tied to the commercial-vehicle cycle: EPS fell 31.9% to SEK 16.0 in 2025 from SEK 23.51 peak, ROIC averages only 9.8% and acquisitions consumed 87% of 10-yr FCF, so growth is cyclical and acquisition-led.

name: AT & S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik AG
reason: Capital-intensive PCB/IC-substrate maker with EPS EUR -1.11 in 2025 (losses in 3 of 11 years), 10-yr ROIC 2.0%, negative cumulative FCF and net debt/EBITDA 4.2x; fails on returns, balance sheet and semiconductor-cycle exposure.

name: Virbac SA
reason: Family-controlled pure-play animal-health franchise (companion-animal skew) with adjusted EPS up from EUR 2.21 (2015) to EUR 18.26 (2025, 23.5% 10-yr CAGR, 16.2% 5-yr), low leverage (0.6x ND/EBITDA) and consensus +13%/+11%/+10%; watch that EBIT margin 14.8% is at the 82nd pctile and recent growth includes bolt-on acquisitions (acq/FCF 0.8).

name: Alm. Brand A/S
reason: Danish P&C insurer whose 10-yr EPS CAGR is only 2.7% (DKK 0.61 to 0.80) with shares compounding +7.5%/yr after the Codan deal, EPS still 60% below its 2021 high, and adjusted/GAAP gap of 70%; ordinary domestic insurer, no ≥7% route.

name: Universal Music Group NV
reason: Durable catalogue/publishing franchise (ROIC ~27%), but GAAP EPS is distorted by stake revaluations (33% adj/GAAP gap; EUR 1.13 in 2024 to 0.83 in 2025), consensus is -3%/+10%/+8% with LTG 6%, and DSP pricing plus AI-generated music are credible 5-yr uncertainties (same call as WMG in the US run).

name: Eckert & Ziegler SE
reason: Isotope sources and radiopharma supply niche with net cash, but EPS more than doubled to EUR 0.78 in 2025 from 0.37 with EBIT margin 24.1% at its 100th pctile, consensus slows to +4%/+8%, and isotope supply, regulatory and radiopharma-pipeline dependence make 5-10 yr earnings hard to forecast.

name: REC Ltd.
reason: State-owned power-sector lender (ROIC 3%, ~9.7x net debt/EBITDA) whose loan book is concentrated in state distribution utilities and whose policy-driven growth is guided by consensus to only +2.5%/+3%/+6%; earnings are set by credit cycle and government policy.

name: LIC Housing Finance Ltd.
reason: LIC-controlled mortgage lender with EPS at a 10-yr high (INR 101.71) after a NIM-driven jump in FY23-24, consensus only +0.2%/+6%/+3.5%, and an undifferentiated spread business vs stronger private peers; fails the through-cycle bank standard.

name: Central Bank of India
reason: State-owned bank with losses in 6 of the last 11 years (EPS INR -26.52 in FY17), 10-yr average ROE -4.1%, shares diluted 18.5%/yr via recapitalisations, and current EPS (INR 5.0) at a post-NPA-cleanup peak; far from best-in-class through cycles.

name: Canara Bank
reason: PSU bank whose EPS (INR 21.19) is at a peak after the credit-cycle recovery, with losses in 3 of the last 11 years, 10-yr average ROE 7.3%, shares up 12.9%/yr from government recapitalisation and merger, and consensus +4%/+9%; fails the through-cycle bank test.

name: Power Finance Corp. Ltd.
reason: State-owned power-sector lender (REC parent) with ROIC 2.2%, ~9.6x net debt/EBITDA, concentrated exposure to state utilities, consensus -3%/+5% and growth tied to government power policy; credit/policy-driven earnings.

name: Bank of India
reason: PSU bank with five straight loss years FY15-19 (EPS INR -78.59 in FY15), 10-yr average ROE 1.0%, 20%/yr share dilution and current EPS INR 23.09 at a cyclical credit peak with consensus -1%/+9%/-3%.

name: Jammu & Kashmir Bank Ltd.
reason: State-government-controlled regional bank with a FY16 loss (EPS INR -32.14), patchy EPS history, 10-yr average ROE 3.9%, 8.6%/yr dilution and no consensus coverage; regional, policy-exposed and at a credit-cycle peak.

name: General Insurance Corporation of India
reason: State-owned reinsurer whose EPS swung from INR 18.13 to -1.06 (FY19) and now sits at a 10-yr high of INR 55.08 on a benign cat/reserving cycle, with 10-yr ROE 12.5% and consensus -0.7%/+8% (LTG 2%); reinsurance results are not forecastable and policy-directed.

name: Bank of Baroda
reason: PSU bank with EPS at a peak (INR 38.72) after the NPA cleanup and merger, losses in FY15/FY17, 10-yr average ROE 7.5%, 8.6%/yr dilution and consensus -11%/+24%; earnings set by credit cycle and state policy.

name: Great Eastern Shipping Co. Ltd.
reason: Tanker/dry-bulk owner whose EPS swung from INR 3.70 (FY18) to INR 190.6 (latest, a 10-yr high) with EBIT margin at the 82nd pctile and consensus -26% in FY2; earnings are set by freight rates.

name: Punjab National Bank
reason: PSU bank with losses in FY15/FY17/FY18 (EPS INR -48.84 in FY17), 10-yr average ROE 0.1%, ~20%/yr share dilution and EPS INR 14.74 at a credit-cycle peak; fails the through-cycle bank standard.

name: Union Bank of India
reason: PSU bank with 10-yr EPS CAGR 1.9% (INR 20.22 to 24.39) despite the recovery, losses FY17-19, 27.7%/yr share dilution from recapitalisation and merger, and 10-yr average ROE 3.3%.

name: Housing & Urban Development Corp. Ltd.
reason: State-owned housing/infrastructure lender lending largely to state agencies, with EPS at a 10-yr high (INR 20.15, +49% in the latest year), ROIC 2.6%, ~11.8x net debt/EBITDA and growth driven by government programmes rather than a franchise.

name: Bank of Maharashtra
reason: PSU bank with losses FY16-18 (EPS INR -14.19 in FY18), 10-yr average ROE 1.5%, 21%/yr share dilution and current EPS INR 9.12 at a post-cleanup peak; growth reflects the credit-cycle rebound, not a durable franchise.
